<reason>B built a durable framing early — the dilemma that A's own "informed, voluntary, coercion-free" definition of consent either matches bare-signature consent (which the pharmacy/landlord cases refute) or already smuggles in the exact extra conditions B is arguing for (which concedes the motion). A never squarely dissolved this dilemma; instead A kept adding machinery (threat/offer distinction, baseline-entitlement theory) to catch new counterexamples, which B correctly flagged in the closing as ad hoc expansion built mid-debate — a charge A's final speech did not directly answer, since it only repeated the "exit collapses into voluntariness" line rather than defending the theory's origin. A's threat/offer and baseline-entitlement moves were clever and gave real analytical traction (especially against the landlord case), and A kept a consistent, principled position on the pharmacy case, but biting the "gouging is ethical, only the epidemic is unjust" bullet is a costly concession that B exploited effectively and repeatedly ("cannot distinguish a merchant from a vulture"). B also grounded claims in ordinary, unnamed legal practice (gouging statutes, unconscionability doctrine) without overclaiming precision, which is legitimate background knowledge rather than fake citation. Execution-wise, A had two clipped turns (opening and rebuttal 2) against B's one clipped closing, a modest additional cost for A. Both sides handled the Pressure Questions and A1/A2 format correctly, but B's landlord question exposed a harder-to-patch weakness in A's theory than A's threshold question exposed in B's, since B's "exit/structured judgment" answer (analogized to legal standards like reasonable care) was a reasonable non-arbitrary response, while A's "it was inside consent all along" answer to the redefinition charge remained more assertion than demonstration.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Rebuttal 1 dilemma ([B2.1]-[B2.3]): forcing A to choose between a thin consent standard refuted by the pharmacy case and a thick standard that concedes consent alone never settles anything — a framing A never fully escaped, culminating in B's closing charge that A's baseline-entitlement fix to the landlord case was built "on the fly" specifically because bare consent couldn't catch it.</best_rebuttal>
